post.title: Korea's main stock index is down 48% since June. Now what?
post.ig:
Korea's main stock index has lost almost half since June.
The Kospi closed at 4,708.54 on Monday, Nov 23, down 3.31% on the day and about 48% below its June 22 record close of 9,114.55 (our math).
Two chipmakers, Samsung Electronics and SK hynix, make up nearly half the index, and the global AI selloff hit both.
Finance Minister Lee Hyoung-il says the government is ready to activate its 10.76 trillion won (about $8 billion) market stabilization fund, set up in 2020 and never used. By our math that's under 1% of the Kospi's market value.
Sources: Korea JoongAng Daily, Yonhap (Nov 23, 2026).
